findings.claim: The new early `if (suppressSourceGeneration is true) return null;` sits before every validation step in GetObjectInfo. The analyzer shares this TypeCollector path, so a `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` type now gets no MsgPack003/004/005/etc. diagnostics at all. The requirement (and ledger L17) asks for the reverse: validation diagnostics must still be reported, and only the generation-specific ones (MsgPack011/016/017) are skipped. Example input: `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] public class Suppressed { public int SuppressedValue { get; set; } }` should produce MsgPack004 but produces nothing on head.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.SuppressedTypeStillReportsMsgPack004. It runs all DiagnosticAnalyzers from the generator assembly over a non-suppressed control type and a SuppressSourceGeneration=true type, each with a public member that lacks [Key]. It asserts MsgPack004 on both; on head the suppressed one is missing.

findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently drop the second member when two members share the same int or string key, and no diagnostic is reported for it. For a non-suppressed type with `[Key(0)] public int A` and `[Key(0)] public int B`, the generated formatter serializes only A. B round-trips as default with no compile-time error, whereas the dynamic resolver rejects duplicate keys at run time. The analyzer crash is turned into silent data loss instead of a reported error.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator test with `[MessagePackObject] public class Dup { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public int B {get;set;} }`. Assert that some error diagnostic is reported, or that the generated formatter contains both A and B. On head neither holds: no diagnostic is reported and the formatter only references A.
